messages:
ian (support): quick heads up — customer #5482 CI deploys are stuck in prod. Step 'release:publish' fails when trying to write audit logs: 403 from logging API.

maria (eng-infra): can you paste the raw error/log? is this cross-project impersonation? @josh fyi.

ian (support): here's the snippet from the runner logs right after the deploy step starts:

```
2026-02-14T18:12:03Z error: status=403 code=PERMISSION_DENIED message=Permission 'logging.logEntries.create' denied for serviceAccount:ci-runner@infra-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
{ "error": { "code": 403, "message": "Permission 'logging.logEntries.create' denied.", "status": "PERMISSION_DENIED" }}
```

ian (support): CI is in infra-project, we impersonate `sa-deployer@prod-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com` to perform production deploys. This started after we moved prod into a separate org unit.

josh (sre): two common causes:
1) the impersonated SA doesn't have the logging role in the project where logs are written (needs roles/logging.logWriter).
2) cross-project impersonation requires the caller to have `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on the impersonated SA and the impersonated SA needs the target project roles.

alice (se): also check token TTL. If the CI job requests very short-lived tokens and the deploy step is long, token might expire mid-request -> 403-ish failures that look like permissions. Do we have TTL set in the runner config?

ian (support): runner config shows `token_ttl: 45s` (yikes) for that job. We also saw intermittent success earlier in the run, then this error.

maria (eng-infra): repro steps to validate from a laptop (safe, non-prod):
1) impersonate the SA (if you have tokenCreator):
```
gcloud auth print-identity-token --impersonate-service-account=sa-deployer@prod-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com --audiences=https://logging.googleapis.com/ | tee /tmp/token
```
2) try a write to the logging API with that token:
```
TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/token)
curl -s -X POST https://logging.googleapis.com/v2/entries:write \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"entries":[{"logName":"projects/prod-project/logs/deploy","resource":{"type":"global"},"textPayload":"test write"}]}' | jq .
```
If you get the same 403 JSON, it's an IAM binding issue for the impersonated SA.

josh (sre): quick fix for prod (apply carefully): grant logging writer to the SA that actually performs the write (the impersonated SA):
```
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding prod-project \
  --member=serviceAccount:sa-deployer@prod-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/logging.logWriter
```
And ensure the CI runner (caller) has token creator on that SA (if using impersonation):
```
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding sa-deployer@prod-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member=serviceAccount:ci-runner@infra-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
```

alice (se): temp workaround while we fix IAM: bump the job token TTL to 1h (or add a token refresh step) and add retry with exponential backoff on the logging write path. That prevents expiry mid-write.

maria (eng-infra): long term: prefer workload identity or cross-project service account with scoped least-priv roles and an explicit `roles/logging.logWriter` binding. Add an IAM condition to limit binder to the deploy job service account (restrict by `request.auth.principal` or by resource name) to keep least privilege.

ian (support): applied roles/logging.logWriter to `sa-deployer@prod-project` and increased TTL to 1h in the pipeline for a canary. Customer reran, deploy succeeded and audit entries show up.

josh (sre): follow-up checklist for infra team:
- Verify `ci-runner` still has `iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on `sa-deployer` (cross-project impersonation).
- Lockdown `sa-deployer` by adding an IAM condition limiting who can impersonate it.
- Add unit test in CI that attempts a small logging write under impersonation to catch regressions.

maria (eng-infra): documented the incident and added the repro steps + commands to the runbook under `support/ci-impersonation-audit-log` (internal). Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

ci-deployer-bot: deploy-check: canary passed for prod cluster-12 at 2026-02-14T19:00:00Z.
